page.title: AI Operating Model Consulting Guide
page.description: Learn what an AI operating model assessment delivers, how consultant and agency outputs differ, which tools support human-in-the-loop workflows, governance steps, and timeline for a first plan.
page.h1: How should AI operating model consulting be run?
page.definition: AI operating model consulting is a structured engagement that evaluates how an organisation embeds artificial intelligence into daily marketing, content and event operations, then delivers an assessment, a prioritised use-case list, a tool choice and a roadmap with governance gates so teams can run human-in-the-loop workflows confidently.
page.quick_answer: Start with a scoped assessment that maps current workflows, identifies high-impact use cases and selects tools before building any automation.

sections.h2: What does an AI operating model assessment deliver?

blocks.p: The assessment produces four concrete outputs that guide the rest of the engagement.

ul: A written assessment of current workflows, data readiness and team skills
A prioritised use-case list ranked by effort, risk and revenue impact
A tool choice matching each use case to a specific platform or model
A roadmap with milestones, owners and review dates

sections.h2: How do consultant and agency outputs differ?

blocks.p: Consultants deliver strategy artefacts while agencies deliver working automations and ongoing support.

head: Dimension
Consultant output
Agency output
rows: Assessment, use-case list, tool choice, roadmap

sections.h2: Which tools support a human-in-the-loop workflow?

blocks.p: A practical stack combines work management, generative AI, creative review, automation hand-offs and reporting.

ul: Asana, Monday.com or ClickUp for workflow tracking and approval gates
ChatGPT or Claude for research, outlines and first drafts
Adobe Firefly or Canva for image variants and brand-compliant assets
Zapier or Make for hand-offs between tools and systems
HubSpot or GA4 for performance reporting and attribution

sections.h2: What governance steps keep AI output safe?

blocks.p: Seven gated steps assign an owner, an output and an approval gate to every AI-assisted task.

ol: Intake: request owner captures brief and success criteria
Brief: strategist defines audience, tone, constraints and data sources
Production: assigned creator runs prompts, reviews raw output
Review: subject expert checks accuracy, brand voice and compliance
Approval: named approver signs off or requests changes
Publishing: operator pushes approved content to live channels
Reporting: analyst logs metrics, feeds insights back to intake

sections.h2: How long does a first operating model plan take?

blocks.p: A first plan runs 90 days and covers six components reviewed monthly.

ul: Governance framework with roles, gates and escalation paths
Tool stack configuration and access controls
Pilot use-case build, test and measure
Team training on prompting, review and approval
Documentation library for prompts, templates and standards
Retrospective to adjust scope, tools or staffing

faq.q: What is the human-in-the-loop rule and why does it matter?
faq.a: The rule states that AI output remains a draft until a named person approves it. This prevents unchecked errors, protects brand voice and creates an audit trail for compliance. Every workflow step must have a designated approver before content goes live.

faq.q: How is pricing structured for AI operating model work?
faq.a: Consultants typically charge a day rate or a fixed project fee for the assessment and roadmap. Agencies quote a fixed build fee for automations plus a monthly retainer for maintenance and support. faq.q: Can West Peek Productions help with implementation?
faq.a: West Peek Productions sets up human-in-the-loop AI workflows for marketing, content and event teams; it is not a general AI consultancy. The team builds the workflow, configures the tool stack and trains internal owners, then hands off with documentation and a support plan.

faq.q: What roles are needed to run the model internally?
faq.a: A minimum viable team includes a workflow owner who manages the board, a prompt engineer or creator who runs the models, a subject expert who reviews output, and an approver who signs off. Larger organisations add a governance lead and an analytics owner for reporting.
